ALPHA-01.coverStory: The Blue Ridge Quarry Reclamation Site is a former limestone quarry under a federal-state abandoned mine land reclamation agreement. Slope stabilization, backfill and groundwater monitoring work continue on the property, and heavy vehicle movements relate to that work. The site is closed to the public because of unstable highwalls and open water. Enquiries should be directed to the regional reclamation field office.

It is not a disaster assistance center; members of the public seeking assistance should contact the published disaster assistance line.

BETA-01.coverStory: The station operates continuous air and surface water quality monitoring for the northern New England region in support of regional environmental programs. Sampling crews and instrument technicians are on site at all hours. The station is not open to the public.

BETA-02.coverStory: This facility manages an underground natural gas storage reservoir and associated compression and monitoring equipment. Restricted access, venting noise and periodic flare testing are normal for gas storage operations. For safety reasons the property is closed to the public; odor or leak reports should be made to the emergency number posted at the gate.

BETA-03.coverStory: The secondary research complex provides contingency laboratory capacity and specimen storage in support of public health programs. High-containment laboratory standards require controlled access, continuous power and on-site security. The complex does not conduct clinical services and is not open to visitors.

BETA-04.coverStory: The station conducts long-term crop, soil and weather research for the northern plains on its surrounding test plots. Seasonal field crews, grain trucks and equipment movements are associated with the research program. The station does not offer public tours.

BETA-05.coverStory: The regional training center provides recurrent and initial training for air traffic and airway facilities personnel, including simulator instruction. Trainees and instructors are on site in shifts through the year. The center is not open to the public.

BETA-06.coverStory: The solar research facility tests concentrating and photovoltaic systems under desert operating conditions. The array field, maintenance buildings and instrumentation are operated by a small resident staff and visiting researchers. Glare and access restrictions apply on the surrounding roads; the facility is not open to visitors.

BETA-07.coverStory: The seismology center operates regional seismic and volcanic monitoring networks and processes data for the Pacific Northwest. Staff maintain field instruments across the region and are on call at all hours. The center is not open to the public.

BETA-08.coverStory: This facility provides logistics, maintenance and security support to activities at the national test site. Vehicle convoys, restricted access and continuous staffing are associated with that support role. Access is restricted to badged personnel.

BETA-09.coverStory: The auxiliary facility provides backup command support and communications routing for the strategic command headquarters. Continuous staffing, restricted access and periodic exercise activity are normal. The facility is not open to the public.

BETA-10.coverStory: The regional response center coordinates federal response resources for the Great Lakes states and hosts interagency planning and exercise activity. Equipment staging, generator testing and shift staffing occur throughout the year. The center is not open to the public.

BETA-11.coverStory: The resource management station supports range, mineral and watershed management for public lands in the Wasatch region. Field crews and survey equipment operate from the station year-round. The station does not provide public services; permit enquiries should be directed to the field office.

BETA-12.coverStory: The hurricane continuity site provides an inland, storm-hardened location from which federal response operations for the Gulf Coast can continue during and after a major storm. Exercises, equipment staging and generator testing are routine. The site is not a shelter and is not open to the public.

divisions.name: Council Secretariat
divisions.mandate: Supports the Core Council in session and between sessions. Keeps the register of distribution copies, prepares agenda and minutes, administers the succession and destruction procedure for Council records, and issues Council resolutions under the Secretary's signature.

divisions.name: Office of Internal Assurance
divisions.mandate: Monitors compliance with security, records and conduct directives across all facilities. Reviews workstation audit trails, opens and closes security incidents, conducts inquiries, and maintains assurance contingencies. Resident Assurance Officers are posted at each ALPHA site.

divisions.name: Records Division
divisions.mandate: Custody, accession, review and destruction of OSC records. Operates the ALPHA-03 records stacks, the agricultural seed collection and the biological sample collection, and maintains the continuity-of-knowledge holdings. Sets records handling rules for all divisions.

divisions.name: Transit Operations
divisions.mandate: Operates the inter-hub rail network and the four regional tram networks from Network Control at ALPHA-01. Issues the working timetable, controls possessions for maintenance, keeps the incident log and submits the certified mileage return.

divisions.name: Facilities Engineering
divisions.mandate: Engineering authority for all facilities and tunnels: structures, life support plant, seals, power distribution and reactor plant engineering. Issues work orders, segment engineering sheets and maintenance schedules.

divisions.name: Personnel & Vetting
divisions.mandate: Recruitment, investigation under the OSC supplement, tier assignment, postings, transfers and probation. Maintains strength accounting and the personnel number register.

divisions.name: Comptroller
divisions.mandate: Programme accounts, cover line-item reconciliation across the four appropriating departments, cost returns to the Council and payroll disbursement.

divisions.name: Communications Security
divisions.mandate: Operates the key distribution network, accredits MERIDIAN workstations, issues tokens and passphrases, and runs the MERIDIAN Service Desk.

divisions.name: Medical Services
divisions.mandate: Clinical services at all staffed facilities, medical readiness standards, pharmaceutical and blood product rotation, and the surgical capability of the network.

divisions.name: Logistics & Reserves
divisions.mandate: Strategic reserves (food, water, medical, energy, armaments), supply movements by tram, generator fuel and reactor operations. Publishes reserve positions and burn-down figures.

divisions.name: Cover Operations
divisions.mandate: Maintains the surface cover facilities and their staffing arrangements, the cover-identity catalogue and the prepared public statements for every facility type.

divisions.name: Security Forces Command
divisions.mandate: Command of security forces at all facilities: post orders, armament issue, access control, guard rotation for DELTA sites, and escort of visitors and consists.

divisions.name: Intelligence & Analysis
divisions.mandate: Operates the intelligence fusion floor at ALPHA-01 and regional analysis cells at BETA sites. Produces threat assessments and the daily continuity summary.

charter.title: Article I: Purpose
charter.text: Continuity is not survival. Continuity is purpose sustained beyond crisis. This infrastructure exists not to shelter us from the end, but to ensure the Republic emerges whole from whatever that end may be.

charter.title: Article II: Membership and Succession
charter.text: The Council shall consist of eleven members, drawn from those offices of government and industry upon which the continuity of the Republic depends: four of Cabinet rank, three who direct the agencies charged with the nation's intelligence and security, two of senior military command, and two from the industries that arm and supply its defense. A seat belongs to the office it represents and passes with that office. When a member departs, the seat stands vacant not for want of a person but for want of a briefing; the successor shall be admitted within thirty days, and the departing member's copy of every Council record shall be destroyed before the successor's copy is issued. No member shall hold two seats, and no seat shall be held in absence.

charter.title: Article III: Authority and Revision
charter.text: The Council is the sole authority of the Office of Strategic Continuity. It acts by a majority of its members present and voting, seven constituting a quorum. This Charter, the Facility Inventory, and every instrument the Council names as governing may be revised by a majority of the full Council and by no lesser body. Authority delegated by the Council is held in trust; it returns to the Council upon the Council's word, without notice and without cause shown.

charter.title: Article IV: Facilities and Custody
charter.text: The facilities of the Office are held in custody for the nation and are the property of no department. Each shall stand under the command of an officer answerable to the Council through the chain established by directive, and each shall keep in ordinary times the readiness it will require in extraordinary ones. No facility shall be surrendered, disclosed or abandoned except by resolution of the Council. The cover under which a facility stands is part of that facility and shall be kept with the same care.

charter.title: Article V: Personnel and Compartmentation
charter.text: Those who serve the Office serve within the tiers and compartments the Council establishes. Each shall know what the work before them requires, and no more; this is not distrust but design. Admission to a compartment is a grant of the Council and may be withdrawn as it was given. The Office shall account for every person in its service, wherever posted or however carried, and the obligations of that service do not lapse with posting, transfer or release.

charter.title: Article VI: Reconstitution
charter.text: Upon the Council's determination that the ordinary institutions of government cannot continue, the Office shall execute the plans of reconstitution it maintains, receive into its facilities those designated essential, and sustain the functions of government until they can be restored in their proper form. The Council shall then sit without adjournment. Its first duty is restoration and not rule, and it shall relinquish each function as the lawful institution able to bear it is restored. The determination itself rests with the Council alone.

charter.title: Article VII: Secrecy and Records
charter.text: The existence of the Office is the first of its secrets. Its governing records shall be kept on paper, in the number of copies the Council directs and in no other form, and each copy shall be accounted for until it is destroyed. No member, officer or employee shall disclose the Office, its facilities or its purpose to any person not admitted to it, under any compulsion. What is not written cannot be lost; what must be written shall be kept as though the Republic depended upon it, for it does.

docNumbering.notes: Four-digit serial, network-wide, never reused. Cited short-form as DIR-0412 in refusals and footers. Revisions keep the number and increment the revision; a replacement takes a new number and a supersession line.
YY = calendar year of issue. Serial resets each January. Issued by the originating division registry.
Formal site-to-site traffic over the key distribution network. Carries a date-time group (DTG) in the heading, e.g. 121430Z MAY 08.
One number per session. Six sessions a year in ordinary times.
Issued under the Secretary's signature.
Articles I-VII.
Seats 01-11. Composition page is OSC-CNL-SEAT-00.
Three-digit form number. Edition date printed in the footer, e.g. OSC-F-131 (EDITION 03/2007).
Issued on submission of a form; serial per form per year.
One per facility. Class pages OSC-FAC-CLS-<CLASS> (e.g. OSC-FAC-CLS-BETA); registry index OSC-FAC-IDX.

SEG-NN segment engineering sheets; NET-<EAS|SOU|MTW|CEN> network sheets; TT-YY-NN working timetable; RS rolling stock register; ENG tunnel engineering; INC-YY-NNN incident log entries; POS-YY-NNN possessions.

Rail consists carry the segment number of their first booked run; tram consists carry the network letters EA, SO, MW or CE. Not a document number; appears on the dispatcher board and in the incident log.
T1-T4 tier pages, PH1-PH5 phases, RATIO ratio model, ORG organisation chart, DIR directory, BR-<code> functional branches, VET vetting supplement, TRF transfer rules.
FOOD, WATER, MED, ENERGY, ARMS, SEED, GENE, and RX-<reactor suffix> reactor status pages.
CAT-<id> categories, SRC-<id> funding sources, REG line-item register, FYNN fiscal years. Line items themselves are LI-NNN (LI-001 to LI-127).
THR-NN threat pages, CSEC construction security, PSEC personnel security, COMM communications, CG classification guide, COV cover catalogue, CTR contractor register.
One per compartment, read in person or on the workstation with an acknowledgement. OSC-CB-010 LANTERN to OSC-CB-016 QUARRY.
Opened by the Office of Internal Assurance. Serial resets each January. Also used as the reference on redactions withheld by OIA.
MERIDIAN Service Desk knowledge base. Four-digit serial.
Internal mail, assigned by the message transfer system on delivery.
Strength and pay reconciliation queries raised to Personnel & Vetting.
Facilities Engineering and Logistics & Reserves work orders (FE-, LR-).
Assigned by Records Division on receipt of any record into the ALPHA-03 stacks.
Workstation audit trail entries; serial per day per workstation group.
Print queue job number; printed on every cover sheet.
GLO glossary, SET settings, MON system monitor, CAL calendar, ABT about this terminal, COL colophon.
The Facility Inventory and Logistics Network. Revision by Council majority only; 11 physical copies.

UNPOSTED_790.notes: R. A. Kessler reconciled the April 2008 pay run against the facility strength returns and found 790 more personnel paid than posted. Query PV-Q-08-0031 raised 17 APR 2008 (OSC-MEM-08-0187). H. Lindqvist closed it 24 APR 2008 (OSC-MEM-08-0203): the category "is maintained in accordance with standing practice and requires no reconciliation action." No directive defining the category is cited. Form OSC-F-131, Unposted Status Declaration, carries no instructions block. Three roster entries (P-3-06-0977, P-4-07-0219, P-3-05-0142) are carried in the category.

TUNNEL_847.notes: The quarterly certified mileage return (signed D. Harker, Transit Operations) reports 847 miles to the Council. Engineering tables (I. Lockhart, Facilities Engineering) carry the segment and network figures. P. Ramanathan, preparing cost-per-mile tables for the Comptroller, wrote "which is it?" against both figures on the routed copy of OSC-MEM-07-0944. The memorandum was returned to file without reply.

CAPACITY_23400.notes: G. Pratt's reserves basis memorandum (OSC-MEM-07-0612) fixes the two definitions: 23,400 is sustained capacity at full reserves, 34,700 is surge berthing. All reserve burn-down figures are stated against the sustained figure.

SEGMENT_04.notes: Segment 04 commissioning sheet signed by O. Garrity, MAR 2007; status NOT IN REVENUE SERVICE with no reason entered. C. Albright's watch notebook records track circuit occupancy on Segment 04 with no consist booked on two occasions; the dispatcher log for the same watches shows a monthly portal seal walk-down possession (OSC-TRN-POS-08-044). R. Tobin, a survey technician on the Segment 04 commissioning crew, has been carried as DETACHED / UNPOSTED since 19 APR 2007.
